brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Kilnroom, the online shop in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: handmade and warm but not rustic or folksy; no pottery wheels, no vase or mug silhouettes, no flames. It must work on a shipping label, a tissue-paper sticker and Instagram. Web and social only; customers in Turkey and Europe.

claim.notes: Üç yönden hiçbiri iki turda kalite kapısını geçmedi (en yakını Witness Cone, kapı skorları 6 ve üzeri ama critic 'sunulamaz' dedi), bu yüzden finalize, export ve gallery yapılmadı.

concepts.title: Witness Cone
readsAs: a shepherd's crook or walking-cane handle
a bent nail or hooded figure (unfortunate: a cane, i.e. age and frailty)
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 two triangles and a hook on a bar, 'AA∩' or pine trees and a cane; horizontal, collapses to tiny text at 16 px. s2 'A∩' letters in a stock round badge (stock 82%), sticker form. s4 tombstone/headstone or mouse-hole door with glyphs cut in: struck (tombstone misread). s3 spike plus shepherd's crook / cane, or the letters 'Ar'/'/r'; strongest silhouette, no tombstone/candle/traffic-cone read. Keep s3. Fix: (1) the bowed cone is a constant-width hook and reads as a cane or umbrella handle; it must taper from a broad base to a point like the standing one, so it reads as the same object slumped. (2) The standing spike is a needle/knife, too sharp for calm and warm: widen the base, soften the tip slightly, consider the real 8-degree lean. (3) Drop the 'k' claim; it does not read as k. (4) Close the gap so they read as a pair; test a shared base edge without adding a shelf bar. Risk: insider object, strangers may not know witness cones; the slump must carry the meaning.

concepts.title: Glaze Line
readsAs: a table or pi sign with drips
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a tombstone / dark doorway with a slit (unfortunate, and the arch-in-a-shop look is the boutique cliche of the moment); s2 a logout/exit door UI icon, struck; s3 a rainbow / tunnel, two-colour dependent, rainbow cliche, struck; s4 a dome lifting off a base - lid opening, the only one that shows an event (the kiln being opened = the drop) rather than a generic arch; s5 a mouse hole or tombstone in a badge, struck. Keep s4: the lifted lid and the wedge of gap are the idea. Risks: it can read as a lunchbox, mailbox, robot head or Pac-man mouth; fix by making the base proportion unmistakably a kiln body (heavier, slightly taller), making the hinge side explicit (gap closed on one side, open on the other, as drawn), and tightening the tilt so it reads as deliberate and precise, not broken. Must hold in one colour - the gap does all the work, keep it >= 16px-safe.

concepts.title: Arch K
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a K cut into an arch tile - the name's initial with cuts, struck; s2 an E / comb / stepped bar chart, different letter, struck; s3 a stock-font K knocked out of a tombstone-shaped app tile - generic monogram-in-container (stock 0.69), gravestone misreading, struck; s4 'Tn' or '7n' - different letters, the arch does not read as a K arm, struck. Different move: stop slicing or boxing the K. Either drop the letter and develop a studio object (kiln lid, witness cone), or build the K from one real kiln structure so the letter is a by-product - e.g. stem as a kiln post with arm and leg as a single bent witness cone, or the K's open angle as the gap of a door left ajar - and draw it as one continuous form, no container, one colour.
